method.critical_control: pytest.ini and conftest.py are UNMODIFIED relative to HEAD (verified with git status --short -- pytest.ini conftest.py, which returned empty). Therefore both arms execute the SAME marker policy and the SAME addopts. Comparing arms under different marker filters was explicitly avoided.
method.no_worktree_checkout_performed: Used the same tree for both arms. Justification: the only working-tree changes are to test files and added tests; the engine/LibCarla edits are outside this repo. Creating a second worktree would have required a large LFS materialisation for no additional signal.
method.what_actually_differs_between_arms: The working tree contains the two restored writer-lock test files (with @pytest.mark.slow correctly applied) plus the new tests/test_import_supervision.py. Arm A and Arm B therefore ran the SAME tree; they serve as a repeatability/host-noise control rather than a before/after code comparison.

duration_variance_explained.observation: Arm B took 1607 s versus Arm A's 1158 s, a 38.9 percent increase, with identical outcomes.
duration_variance_explained.cause: Host contention, not a code or test change. A live cook (UE4Editor PID 5344) and its ShaderCompileWorker children were consuming CPU throughout both arms; the workers were still active at the end of Arm B (PIDs 25288, 29864). The suite contains real multiprocess stress tests (349.60 s and 145.21 s single-test maxima) whose wall time is highly sensitive to available cores.
duration_variance_explained.evidence_that_it_is_not_a_selection_chan: Identical passed/failed/skipped/deselected counts in both arms. A selection change would alter counts, not merely duration.

stress_tests_are_not_excluded.concern: The brief warned that adding -m 'not slow' might silently remove stress coverage.
stress_tests_are_not_excluded.finding: The stress tests ARE included in the 5213. The default pytest.ini addopts are '-v --tb=short --strict-markers' with NO -m filter, so a bare run selects everything. Deselected = 0 in both arms.
stress_tests_are_not_excluded.explicit_stress_mode_still_recommended: Yes, as a convenience split only. See PYTEST_EXECUTION_POLICY.json. It must not replace the bare run in release assurance.

collection_state.note: Two test files previously failed to collect (C# source injected into Python test bodies). Both were restored from HEAD in this convergence wave, recovering 12 tests. Before the fix: 5205 items / 2 errors / Interrupted. After: 5217 items collected for tests/ with 0 errors; the 5219 total includes the two deselected-by-default items in the wider testpaths.

tests_repaired: tests/unit/test_a1_a2_path_and_frame_resolution.py::test_missing_osm2world_fails_precisely (made hermetic; was failing due to repo layout)

not_claimed: No performance regression is claimed or ruled out from a single pair of runs on a loaded host; duration comparison is not reliable here and only outcome counts are treated as evidence.

The wider pytest.ini testpaths (ultimate_pipeline/tests, tests/phase_q, tests/carla_tools outside tests/, tests/opendrive_geometry, tests/quality, tests/roadrunner, tests/topology) were not swept; this audit covers the tests/ directory.
